misconception_pool.misconception: Halftone printing creates gray shades by mixing black ink with white ink in different ratios inside the press fountain.
misconception_pool.fact: Halftone screens simulate shades of gray by printing tiny solid black dots of varying sizes spaced across white paper.

misconception_pool.misconception: Enlarging a 72-PPI web graphic to twelve inches wide in page layout software automatically adds sharp print detail.
misconception_pool.fact: Scaling up a low-resolution raster image stretches existing pixels over a larger area, producing blurry or jagged edges in print.

misconception_pool.misconception: Vector illustrations store images as a fixed grid of colored pixels that lose clarity whenever the art is resized.
misconception_pool.fact: Vector graphics store shapes as mathematical paths and curves that scale to any dimension without losing edge sharpness.

misconception_pool.misconception: RGB color files sent directly to a four-color commercial press will match the bright neon colors seen on a monitor.
misconception_pool.fact: Commercial presses print with subtractive CMYK inks, which have a smaller color gamut than additive RGB computer monitors.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Graphic Arts Requirement 1, how do the four traditional printing processes (relief, intaglio, planographic, and porous) transfer ink to a substrate?
options: A. All four processes carve deep grooves into wooden blocks and melt solid wax crayons onto the paper using laser beams.
B. Offset lithography forces ink through a woven silk mesh, while screen printing etches microscopic wells into a heavy copper cylinder.
C. Relief prints from raised surfaces, gravure/intaglio prints from recessed ink-filled cells etched into a cylinder.
D. Gravure uses raised rubber stamps for corrugated cardboard, while flexography uses only home inkjet cartridges.
choices: A. All four processes carve deep grooves into wooden blocks and melt solid wax crayons onto the paper using laser beams.
B. Offset lithography forces ink through a woven silk mesh, while screen printing etches microscopic wells into a heavy copper cylinder.
C. Relief prints from raised surfaces, gravure/intaglio prints from recessed ink-filled cells etched into a cylinder.
D. Gravure uses raised rubber stamps for corrugated cardboard, while flexography uses only home inkjet cartridges.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Relief prints from raised surfaces, gravure/intaglio prints from recessed ink-filled cells etched into a cylinder, offset lithography prints from a flat plate using the mutual repulsion of oil-based ink and water, and screen printing squeegees ink through open mesh areas of a stencil.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Graphic Arts Requirement 1 differentiates printing methods by image carrier geometry: raised image areas (relief/flexography), recessed wells (intaglio/gravure), flat chemically treated plates (offset lithography), and stencil mesh openings (screen printing), alongside modern digital printing.
